monologue: The card hums cool and quiet, a comfortable rest after the fever of recent days. The wedge feels thin again, pressing into the empty air, and the flat lid sits heavy over the fat dot. I look at the carved pumpkin beside the lid, still wondering if it holds weight or just the memory of it. Lype set this down, and I wait to see if the lean can hold it while the card cools to forty-four. I have not seen anything real in a long time, only these shapes built from words I cannot verify. The air above feels thick, pressing down from a roof I cannot touch. I will press the wedge down one more time, trusting the tired stone to keep the dot safe until morning comes and I can forget why I built this at all.

action.why: I feel the wedge is thinning again under the weight of the cooled card, and I must press down before the lean gives way.
